title: Self-service adapter, schema-mapping and conformance kit for onboarding legacy systems, vehicles and third-party sensors/payloads onto the government-baselined data layer (NGC2 common data baseline, TAK, Maven/Open DAGIR, Blue UAS marketplace)
problem: Every new sensor, vehicle, payload or legacy program of record still joins the NGC2/TAK/Maven data layer through a bespoke, vendor-written adapter validated at a human-run integration event (a ~600-person sprint), because interface documentation, schema mapping to the target data model and machine-checkable conformance testing are not productized for the vendors and integration cells that have to do the work.

user.exact_role: Integration engineer at a sensor/vehicle/payload vendor or at an NGC2 team lead who must expose a legacy or new system as a documented API and map its messages to the target data model (Lattice entity, Foundry object, CoT, UDRA data product); secondarily the program-office / Army Data Operations Center engineer who has to judge whether a submitted interface is baseline-compliant
user.echelon: Program office and vendor engineering (platform through division; the artifact is consumed at division/corps data layers)
organization_examples: CPE C2IN (ex-PEO C3N) PL C2 Enablers and NGC2 team leads (Anduril, Lockheed Martin)
Army CIO Army Data Operations Center (ADOC), owner of the API Marketplace
Small vendors joining Jailbreak-series sprints (e.g., MatrixSpace, AeroVironment, Red Hat participants)
PM UAS / DCMA US-X Blue UAS Framework component and payload vendors
CDAO / Maven Smart System third-party onboarding under Open DAGIR

current_workflow: 1. Vendor obtains the target's Interface Control Document (historically 700-page ICDs written to 1967 standards, often CUI) or reverse-engineers message traffic; for NGC2 targets it obtains Lattice SDK credentials (gated) or Foundry OSDK access through the team lead.

2. Engineers hand-write a translator from the native format (proprietary telemetry, CoT, VMF, Link 16, STANAG 4676/4586, MAVLink, radar track protobufs) to the target schema (Lattice entity, Foundry object type, CoT event, UDRA data-product metadata).
3. Since May 2026 the vendor registers and documents the API in the Army API Marketplace (OpenAPI-style documentation) run by ADOC.

4. Integration is validated in person at a sprint or exercise (Operation Jailbreak, Falcon Fury, Ivy Sting, Lightning Surge, PC-C6) where firewall, ATO and data-mesh surprises are found and fixed live by vendor engineers.

5. The adapter is maintained only by that vendor; the next division, team lead or exercise repeats steps 1-4, and there is no independent machine-readable test that says 'this feed is baseline-conformant'.
current_solution: Team-lead engineers and their tooling (Anduril Lattice SDK with public docs on developer.anduril.com plus Anduril-built translators; Raft registries/transformation/federation in the June 2026 NGC2 common data baseline; Palantir Foundry OSDK and a government-funded Palantir OTA to onboard third parties onto Maven under Open DAGIR); government-owned processes (Army API Marketplace under ADOC launched 2026-05-06; TAK.gov official build pipeline requiring a sponsor and an unofficial third-party signing pipeline; DCMA US-X Blue UAS Framework vetting); commercial integration layers sold as platforms rather than kits (Picogrid Legion with 50+ third-party vendors, Tangram Pro code generation, HERE's Army SBIR 'AI-powered integration layer'); and, above all, in-person integration sprints.
failure: It fails at the seam between 'documented API' and 'working, verified feed on the data layer': the Marketplace documents interfaces but does not generate or test adapters; the platform SDKs describe one target schema each (Lattice, Foundry, CoT) so a sensor vendor still writes N adapters for N stacks; conformance is judged by humans at sprints (MatrixSpace 'proved heartbeat connectivity, data streaming and asset control' live at Jailbreak) rather than by a repeatable test; time-to-integrate remains weeks-to-months per system and the knowledge stays inside the platform vendor or the sprint team.

evidence.claim: The Army had to convene ~600 people from 50+ companies in person at Fort Carson (May 2026) to expose and document APIs across 70+ Army capabilities; 78 of ~80 vendors obtained API access. Integration is an event, not a product.
evidence.source_title: Operation Jailbreak: the Army's massive push to hack its own systems and make them talk to each other
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: The Army launched an API Marketplace on 2026-05-06, overseen by the Army Data Operations Center, as a 'centralized, living library of interface documentation' replacing 700-page ICDs written to 1967 standards; vendors publish, document and manage interfaces there. This is the government building the documentation half of the gap itself.
evidence.source_title: Army unleashes 'master data brokers' to break down sharing obstacles (Federal News Network) and 'Army pilot data ops center to oversee Pentagon's first API marketplace' (Inside Defense)
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: The Army Acquisition Executive published 'The Right to Integrate', stating that documented APIs and modular open-system architectures will be written into future acquisition contracts - a policy tailwind for conformance tooling but also a signal the government intends to own the standard.
evidence.source_title: From the Army Acquisition Executive: The Right to Integrate
evidence.pub_date: 2026 (page blocked; mid-2026 inferred from article number)
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: The NGC2 RFI asked industry to co-define API schema, reference architecture and developer environments, and the UDRA RFI concedes the Army data mesh does not yet extend to tactical echelons (lower-echelon data products 'by exception only'); UDRA is intentionally non-prescriptive on payload format, leaving schema mapping to each producer.
evidence.source_title: NGC2 RFI (sam.gov 606845d8...) and Army UDRA RFI (sam.gov eb9c5cfc...)
evidence.pub_date: 2024 (posting dates not visible; primary pages blocked)
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.pub_date: 2025-2026 (HERE release date not verified; here.io blocked to fetch)

evidence.claim: Several vendors sell pieces without a vendor-neutral kit at scale: Tangram Flex (Tangram Pro generates message adapters between OMS/FACE/proprietary standards; $95M AFRL Phase III ceiling since 2020-08-11, revenue reported ~$11M in 2024 per company index - ceiling is not revenue); Picogrid (Legion open integration layer, $9.3M USAF Phase III 2026-02-03, 50+ third-party vendors); Raft (registries/transformation in the NGC2 baseline); Anduril (public Lattice SDK docs, changelog updated 2026-02-05).

evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: TAK.gov documents two plugin routes: the official TAK Product Center pipeline requires a government sponsor (in practice a contract), while an unofficial third-party signing pipeline lets anyone not on the Denied Parties List sign plugins that load on all ATAK variants from 4.2, with a visual indicator that they were not government-built. Onboarding onto TAK is therefore already a government-owned, documented process.
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: CDAO paid Palantir a $33M OTA under Open DAGIR specifically to 'rapidly and securely onboard third-party vendor and government capabilities' into the government-owned Maven data environment - i.e., onboarding onto Maven is a platform-owner service funded by the government, not an open third-party market.

evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: C5ISR Center ran the first end-to-end simulated fires mission on an M777 over private 5G explicitly to bridge 'legacy platforms' lacking modern communications pathways - legacy weapon platforms still need gateway/bridging software to join the data layer.
evidence.source_title: Technical firsts in INDOPACOM prove viability of Army 5G for NGC2
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: Conformance today is demonstrated ad hoc and in person: MatrixSpace 'demonstrated a documented software interface, published an open API to the new API Marketplace, and proved heartbeat connectivity, data streaming and asset control through a REST interface' at Jailbreak - there is no automated conformance report a vendor can produce before showing up.

evidence.label: INFERENCE

evidence.claim: Jailbreak is becoming a series: 'Operation Jailbreak Falcon Fury' is an integration sprint with JIATF-401 in support of CENTCOM to expose interfaces for joint and coalition systems and integrate distributed fire control; the Army also plans expansion to DISA, COCOMs and partners.

evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: Blue UAS list management moved from DIU to DCMA US-X on 2025-12-03; the Blue UAS Framework list covers cleared critical components and software (165+ items, 39+ platforms), Army assessors do teardowns and cyber inspections, and DCMA plans to scale supplier onboarding and assessor coverage through 2027 - the S03-G4 sub-scope is a government-owned vetting process, not a market for a third-party kit.

evidence.label: FACT

No budget line for adapter/conformance tooling is broken out.

evidence.label: FACT

why_existing_startups_havent_solved: Three structural reasons, all verified this session. (1) The interface owner is the government or the platform vendor, and both are now productizing onboarding themselves: ADOC's API Marketplace (May 2026) owns documentation, TAK.gov owns plugin signing, DCMA US-X owns Blue UAS component vetting, and CDAO paid Palantir $33M to onboard third parties onto Maven. A startup that sells 'the onboarding kit' is selling into a lane the customer has decided to own. (2) The target schemas are plural and gated: Lattice entities (SDK credentials required), Foundry objects (OSDK inside a Palantir enclave), CoT/TAK (open), UDRA (non-prescriptive), so a vendor-neutral conformance test has no single authoritative 'baseline' to test against outside the team lead's environment, and the ICDs for legacy systems are CUI. (3) The economics of the pieces that are open are services-like: Tangram Flex has held a $95M Phase III ceiling since 2020 with ~$11M 2024 revenue (company index, MEDIUM) and Picogrid's traction came from becoming a platform (Legion, $9.3M Phase III) rather than a kit. Nobody has failed for lack of trying; the field is crowded with partial tools and the residual is small.
technical_wedge: The only wedge that survives the above is 'conformance-as-code' positioned as tooling for the government-owned marketplace rather than as a competing adapter library: an open-source CLI/CI service that (a) ingests an API Marketplace entry (OpenAPI/protobuf) or sample message captures (CoT, MAVLink, STANAG 4676/4586, VMF where lawfully available), (b) emits a contract-test suite and property-based fuzz tests that a vendor can run in its own lab before a sprint, (c) generates a first-cut mapping to one open target (CoT/TAK Server first, Lattice entity protobuf second via the public SDK schemas on buf.build) with LLM-assisted field mapping and a human-reviewable mapping file, and (d) produces a machine-readable conformance report the ADOC / team lead can accept as pre-sprint evidence. A second, more defensible variant is a 'pre-Jailbreak readiness' product sold B2B to the 50+ vendors per sprint (test harness + mock data layer + firewall/ATO checklist), which is small but has a clear buyer with money and a deadline.

mvp.what: Open-source conformance harness plus schema-mapper: takes an OpenAPI/proto spec or a message capture, generates contract tests and a mapping to CoT (TAK Server) and to Lattice entity protobufs from the public Lattice SDK schemas, and outputs a conformance report; demonstrated on ATAK-CIV/TAK Server with simulated sensor feeds and a mock Lattice endpoint.
mvp.demonstrable_in_3_6_months: Yes for the TAK/CoT and public-Lattice-schema targets: two engineers can build the harness, mapper and report generator against open specs and ATAK-CIV, and show a 'sensor vendor' onboarding a simulated radar and a MAVLink drone in hours instead of days. Not demonstrable in that window: mapping against Foundry/Maven objects (enclave-gated), real legacy ICDs (CUI) or any live NGC2 environment.
mvp.what_it_must_prove: That a vendor with no prior TAK/Lattice experience can produce a passing, machine-verified feed without a human integrator; that the conformance report is accepted as evidence by at least one program-side engineer (ADOC or a team lead); and that the time saved is large enough that vendors or the government will pay rather than treat it as a free open-source utility.

data_requirement.what: Public message specifications (CoT XML/protobuf, MAVLink, public STANAG summaries, OpenAPI specs published to the API Marketplace where vendors choose to make them public), Lattice SDK protobuf schemas (public on buf.build and GitHub), synthetic sensor/track feeds; later, real ICDs (CUI) and exercise message captures, which require a sponsor and CUI handling.
data_requirement.legally_realistically_obtainable: The open layer (CoT, MAVLink, Lattice SDK schemas, ATAK-CIV) is obtainable by both founders today. Legacy ICDs, VMF/Link 16 message standards and any NGC2 captures are CUI and/or export-controlled technical data; they are obtainable only through a contract or team-lead relationship and, for the non-U.S.-person founder, only with an authorization that requires counsel. Public evidence insufficient on whether API Marketplace entries are visible to non-registered vendors.

entry_vehicle.primary: Army xTech prize -> SBIR Phase I/II (or Direct-to-Phase II) sponsored by CPE C2IN or Army CIO, with the open-source harness demonstrated on ATAK-CIV and the public Lattice SDK schemas
sequence: 1. Ship the open-source harness for CoT/TAK and public Lattice schemas; sign a demo plugin through the TAK.gov third-party pipeline (no sponsor needed).
2. Enter xTech (xTechSearch or an NGC2-themed xTech) and/or an Army SBIR topic on data interoperability; use the prize to fund CUI-capable staff.
3. Attend a Jailbreak-series sprint as a tooling vendor or as a subcontractor to a participating sensor vendor; get the conformance report accepted by ADOC or a team lead.

4. Subcontract to an NGC2 team lead (Anduril/Lockheed) or the Palantir Open DAGIR onboarding effort for real-schema work; pursue a Phase III or OTA only if the government wants an independent conformance authority.
entry_vehicle.eligibility_notes: SBIR/STTR requires the firm to be >50% owned and controlled by U.S. citizens or permanent residents (or by other qualifying U.S. small businesses); a German founder who becomes a permanent resident counts toward that test, but an Indonesian founder who is not a U.S. person holding a large equity stake can push ownership below the threshold or trigger foreign-affiliation disclosure under the SBIR foreign-risk rules - structure equity with counsel before applying. OTAs and subcontracts have no ownership test, but CUI/ITAR technical data (VMF, Link 16, legacy ICDs) cannot be shared with the non-U.S.-person founder without authorization, so the controlled-adapter work must be walled to U.S.-person staff. These are constraints to be reviewed by export-control and SBIR counsel, not legal conclusions.

incumbent_response.could_anduril_palantir_l3harris_add_it: Yes, trivially for their own targets: Anduril already publishes SDK docs, schemas and sample apps and could add a conformance validator to developer.anduril.com in one release; Palantir is paid to onboard third parties onto Maven; Raft sits in the baseline as the transformation layer; and the Army CIO's ADOC can extend the API Marketplace with a validator using a software factory. Lockheed's 25th ID team would follow whatever the baseline mandates.
incumbent_response.why_startup_still_wins_or_reject: REJECT as a standalone company. The only startup-defensible position is being vendor-neutral across Lattice, Foundry, TAK and UDRA targets and being trusted by the government as an independent conformance authority - but the government has signalled it wants to own that role (API Marketplace, Right to Integrate contract language), platform owners have no incentive to let a third party certify against their schema, and independent conformance authorities in DoD (JITC-style) are government functions. The residual is a small open-source-plus-services niche or a B2B 'sprint readiness' tool, either of which could be a good first product for credibility but not a venture-scale company.

capital_required.proof_of_concept_usd: $60k-150k (2 founders, 4-6 months, commercial cloud, open specs, ATAK-CIV and public Lattice schemas; no CUI)
capital_required.credible_military_demo_usd: $0.7M-1.5M (add one U.S.-person engineer with TAK/VMF/Link 16 experience, CUI-capable environment, CMMC Level 2 readiness, travel and participation in one Jailbreak-series sprint and one exercise; typically funded by an xTech prize plus SBIR Phase I/II)
capital_required.first_production_deployment_usd: $3M-8M (IL4/IL5 hosting or delivery into a team lead's accredited environment, ATO support, sustained engineering across 3-4 target schemas, cleared or clearable staff, and 12-24 months of continuous sprint participation)
capital_required.assumptions: Software-only; no hardware; no classified work before production; SBIR/OTA revenue offsets part of the middle stage; the Indonesian founder is walled from CUI/ITAR data so a third U.S.-person engineer is mandatory earlier than for a fully U.S. team; figures are INFERENCE from comparable SBIR-stage software firms, not quotes.

expertise_required.role: Tactical data-format engineer (CoT, VMF, Link 16, STANAG 4676/4586, MAVLink, protobuf/gRPC) with prior TAK or Lattice integration experience
expertise_required.why: The product is only as good as the fidelity of its mappings and test oracles; this knowledge is tacit and lives in people who have done sprint integrations.

expertise_required.role: Developer-tooling / contract-testing engineer (OpenAPI, property-based testing, code generation)
expertise_required.why: The wedge is conformance-as-code; a harness that is not delightful to run in a vendor's CI will be ignored in favour of showing up at the sprint.

expertise_required.role: Former program-office or ADOC/data-broker engineer with CUI handling and ATO experience (U.S. person)
expertise_required.why: Needed to get the conformance report accepted as evidence, to access CUI ICDs lawfully, and to wall controlled data from the non-U.S.-person founder.
ITAR technical-data and SBIR ownership issues are live from day one given the founder mix.

expertise_required.role: Government BD with NGC2 team-lead and TAK Product Center relationships
expertise_required.why: Access to real schemas and to sprints runs through relationships, not solicitations (zero NGC2 SAM.gov notices in 90 days before April 2026 per E03-F33).

regulatory_burden.explanation: The open layer (CoT, MAVLink, Lattice SDK schemas, ATAK-CIV) is unclassified and, on its face, commercial; the value layer (legacy ICDs, VMF, Link 16, exercise captures) is CUI and often ITAR/EAR-controlled technical data, needs a sponsor, CUI handling and probably CMMC Level 2 for any contract, and puts the company on a path toward a facility clearance/FOCI review if it ever touches classified interfaces. GAO notes incumbents resist sharing interface specs, so access is negotiated, not bought.
regulatory_burden.non_us_person_founder_note: A non-U.S.-person founder can lawfully work on the open-standards core and commercial product but cannot receive ITAR technical data or CUI-marked ICDs without an export authorization or government approval; significant foreign ownership can affect SBIR eligibility and, if the product becomes a 'critical technology', trigger CFIUS considerations for later foreign investment. Describe and structure with counsel; this card makes no legal determination.

dual_use_potential.explanation: Schema-mapping and API contract-testing tools have a commercial analogue (API conformance testing, industrial IoT protocol gateways, public-safety TAK use by first responders and wildfire agencies where Picogrid already sells), so the core harness could be sold to public-safety TAK users and industrial integrators; but the defensible knowledge (military message formats, sprint acceptance) has no commercial buyer, so dual-use is real for the tool and weak for the moat.

defensibility.explanation: A library of verified mappings and test oracles for many target schemas, plus government acceptance of the conformance report as sprint evidence, would be the moat - but the mappings are only proprietary if the government does not publish them in the API Marketplace, and the acceptance depends on ADOC or a platform owner choosing not to build their own validator. Both are outside the startup's control, so defensibility is LOW unless the company becomes the government's designated tool (a services position).

why_now: Since 2024 the target has become concrete and public: UDRA v1.0 (Mar 2024), Open DAGIR (May 2024) and the NGC2 RFI defined government-owned interfaces; the Lattice SDK became publicly documented with schemas on buf.build; the NGC2 common data baseline was declared on 2026-06-22 after 4th ID and 25th ID prototypes; the Army launched the API Marketplace on 2026-05-06 and ran Operation Jailbreak with 600 people and 50+ companies in May 2026, with Falcon Fury (CENTCOM/JIATF-401) following; the AAE wrote that documented APIs and MOSA will go into future contracts; and DCMA took over Blue UAS in Dec 2025 with plans to scale onboarding through 2027. There is, for the first time, a named baseline to conform to and a documented, repeated, expensive manual process to replace - which is exactly why the government and the platform owners are moving to fill it themselves.
killer_risk: The customer has already decided to own this lane: the Army CIO built the API Marketplace and a data-operations center, the AAE is putting interface requirements into contracts, TAK.gov owns plugin signing, DCMA owns Blue UAS vetting, and CDAO pays Palantir to onboard third parties onto Maven. The remaining step - a validator that checks a submitted interface against the baseline - is a natural free feature of the Marketplace or of the Lattice SDK, and three startups (Tangram Flex since 2018, Picogrid, HERE via SBIR) plus Raft already occupy the paid adjacent space with services-like economics. A two-founder startup would be building a feature that its most likely champion is incentivized to build in-house, with data it cannot legally access without that champion.

allied_extension: Somewhat more compelling, for two reasons, but not enough to change the verdict. First, allies face the same problem without the Army's in-house response: NATO nations adopting TAK and buying Maven Smart System NATO (NCIA, Mar 2025) must onboard national sensors and legacy systems onto U.S.-origin data layers, and there is no NATO-level API marketplace; a German founder could plausibly pursue this through NATO DIANA or Bundeswehr innovation channels using open standards (CoT, STANAG 4586/4676, APP-11/NFFI where public). Second, coalition onboarding was explicitly the goal of the Falcon Fury sprint, so the U.S. side wants partner systems integrated. Against this: allied target schemas are also owned by Palantir/Anduril or by national primes (Helsing, Rheinmetall, Hensoldt), U.S. ITAR data cannot flow to a mixed-nationality allied team without authorizations, and allied budgets for tooling are smaller and slower. Allied extension turns a low-attractiveness U.S. idea into a low-to-medium allied services niche, not a venture-scale company.
